notes: SHIP v1.14.367 - ART DROP: the 9 curated OPS wall rasters install as final bytes. Asset-only ship. .366 wired the nine wall cells to background art, but the webp files in the repo were stale bytes from three different eras - a provenance check showed sops and power last touched at v1.14.160 (2026-07-01), bom/manifest/portmap at v1.14.185 (2026-07-05), and rackmap/burndown/audits/optics at v1.14.319 (2026-07-20). Nothing newer had ever landed: neither .365 nor .366 contained a single webp, no webp anywhere in the repo was untracked or uncommitted, and all nine were byte-clean against HEAD. The wall was therefore rendering a mix of two generations of art, which is why some cells looked more wrong than others. This ship replaces all nine with the curated set. FILENAMES DO NOT CHANGE, so the cache version bump is what actually pushes the new bytes to devices: an unchanged URL whose bytes changed is served from the old service-worker cache indefinitely otherwise, which is the same offline-only, invisible-online failure mode that governs every asset ship here. VERIFICATION BEFORE ANYTHING WAS WRITTEN. Each of the nine base64 blocks was decoded in memory and checked on three independent axes - exact byte length against the length declared in the drop, sha256 against the checksum declared per file, and RIFF/WEBP magic to confirm the decoded bytes really are a WebP rather than something that merely decoded cleanly. All twenty-seven checks passed, and only then were the files written. The decode step was deliberately kept out of the assistant's context: the drop document is roughly 179k tokens of base64, and it was parsed by script rather than read, so no byte of art passed through a lossy path. AN EXTRA CHECK THE DROP DID NOT ASK FOR: all nine were confirmed 256x256 and 1:1. This matters because .366's per-shell fit ruling was derived from a square-source assumption - phone keeps cover because a 1:1 source still shows 82% of itself in a 107x88 cell, desk takes contain because a 3.95:1 cell would otherwise discard 75% of a square icon's height. Had any new render arrived at a different aspect, that ruling would have needed re-deriving rather than inheriting. It did not: every file is 256x256 lossy VP8, so .366's cover/contain split remains exactly correct and no CSS changed. SIZES ALL MOVED, IN BOTH DIRECTIONS - bom 13126 to 13784, manifest 15812 to 20654, portmap 15442 to 13742, rackmap 25826 to 14824, sops 10398 to 14486, burndown 21396 to 15102, audits 26238 to 15976, power 12558 from 17606, optics 28202 to 17494. Net the icon set got smaller by about 47 KB, which every cold install now saves. Zero of the nine were already identical, confirming the drop is genuinely new art rather than a re-issue of what was already there. SCOPE: nine asset files plus the three stamps. No wiring, no CSS, no DEPLOY_TOOLS, no precache edit - all nine filenames were already in PRECACHE_URLS and none changed, so sw.js moves by its cache version alone. DELIBERATE DEVIATION FROM THE DROP'S STEP 4, which reads as though the assets and the stamps could be two commits: they are ONE commit here. Splitting them would create an intermediate commit carrying new bytes under the old cache version, and if that commit ever reached Pages, every field device would keep serving the stale images from cache while the repo looked correct. The three-stamp lockstep exists precisely to make that state unrepresentable. DEVICE-VERIFY: (1) badge reads v1.14.367. (2) The SW must actually turn over before any of this is visible - fully quit the PWA (swipe it out of the app switcher, not background it) and relaunch; the first launch after a ship routinely still serves the old cache. Do NOT clear website data to force it, that destroys the Master file and every deployment, SOP, audit and optic record in localStorage. (3) Check AUDITS and BURNDOWN first as the drop advises - they carried the oldest stale vintage, so the before/after is clearest there. (4) All nine cells must still tap through; art must never cost a door. (5) Both shells: phone art fills the cell, desk shows the whole icon centred and sharp. ROLLBACK: revert this commit - restores all nine previous rasters and the stamps together.
